To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
image-guided biopsy of suspected metastasis in patients with breast or non-breast cancer should be considered to optimize patient management.

biopsy of suspected metastasis in patients with breast or other cancer is recommended in practice guidelines but not always performed, because of the cost or invasiveness of biopsy, and that biopsy can confirm the presence or absence of cancer, reveal unsuspected second malignancy, or confirm expression of biomarker, all of which may aid in the optimal management of cancer.
biopsy of suspected breast metastases is recommended in the NCCN clinical practice guidelines and that image-guided biopsy has significantly increased the accuracy and decreased the risk of biopsy.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of novel methods and algorithms for the analysis of medical image data.
the development of new and improved methods for the treatment of breast cancer and other cancers, and the application of these techniques in clinical trials and in the clinic.
the development and evaluation of a biopsy algorithm for suspected metastases.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
biopsy is the gold standard to diagnose metastatic breast cancer.
biopsy of suspected metastatic lesions is recommended for patients with breast cancer and is best done by image-guided biopsy.
biopsy should be performed in patients with breast metastases when it is clinically indicated, and the biopsy results can impact on clinical management.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
biopsy of suspected metastatic breast cancer lesions is recommended for all patients with newly diagnosed metastatic disease.
biopsy of suspected metastatic breast cancer is an important procedure that is often not performed in clinical practice.
image-guided biopsy of metastases is safe and can be performed with minimal morbidity.
The main takeaway from our work is that
biopsy of metastatic sites is an important component of the management of patients with breast cancer.
biopsy of suspected metastatic disease in patients with breast and other cancers should be considered a standard of care.
the decision to biopsy should be based on a careful consideration of the potential benefits and harms of biopsy, as well as the patient’s preferences and values.
